+# Manage exemptions - Microsoft Security Exposure Management | Microsoft Learn
+
+Exemptions help security teams focus on the risks that require action while maintaining a governed record of findings that don't require remediation. Use an exemption when a finding has been reviewed and determined to be a false positive, covered by another control, temporarily deferred, or accepted as risk. Each exemption records its scope, matching conditions, justification, and review period, helping your organization reduce operational noise without losing visibility or accountability.
+
+Note
+
+Exemptions are currently available only for **Cloud resources**.
+
+For **Devices**, use the **Exception options** directly from the recommendation experience.
+
+For **SaaS Apps, Identities, and Data**, use **Edit Status & Action Plan** on the recommendation as the alternative way to manage exemptions.
+
+[![Screenshot showing the Exemptions tab on the Policies page in the Microsoft Defender portal.](media/manage-exemptions-defender/manage-exemptions.png)](media/manage-exemptions-defender/manage-exemptions.png#lightbox)
+
+## Why use exemptions?
+
+Exemptions provide a structured alternative to informally suppressing a security finding. They help organizations:
+
+- Focus remediation resources on security findings that require action.
+- Apply a documented risk decision consistently across the relevant scope.
+- Reduce repetitive work by managing exceptions through centralized rules.
+- Record the justification and supporting context needed for governance, audit, and compliance.
+- Reassess accepted risks through expiration dates and lifecycle review.
+- Preserve the security context of exempted findings in investigation and attack-path experiences.
+
+## Use cases
+
+Create an exemption after a finding has been generated and reviewed, and your organization determines that remediation is not currently required. Common scenarios include:
+
+- The finding is a false positive.
+- The organization reviewed and accepted the risk.
+- A third-party control addresses the risk.
+- An alternative mitigation is already in place.
+- Remediation is deferred for a documented business or technical reason.
+
+## Remove a rule or create an exemption?
+
+Both recommendation policies and exemptions allow you to control recommendation behavior, but they serve different governance purposes. Use a policy change when a recommendation should not be evaluated for a specific scope. Use an exemption when the recommendation remains valid, but remediation is temporarily not required and should be tracked for governance, audit, or compliance purposes.
+
+| Action | What it does | Choose it when |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Remove the rule from a policy | Stops the rule from generating recommendations and findings for the selected policy scope. Assets within that scope will no longer be evaluated against the rule. | The recommendation is not relevant for the selected scope and should never apply there. This is a long-term policy decision that defines which security controls should be evaluated. Learn more in [Manage posture policies](manage-posture-policies-defender). |
+| Create an exemption | Keeps the rule active and continues evaluating the finding, but marks matching findings as **Exempted** for the approved scope and review period. | The finding is valid, but remediation is temporarily postponed or accepted as an exception. Exemption preserves visibility, justification, ownership, and review tracking for governance, audit, and compliance needs. |
+
+## Before you begin
+
+### Verify that an environment is managed in Defender
+
+Exemptions created in Defender apply only to assets that belong to environments managed in Defender. You can verify the management location in either of the following ways:
+
+- From the recommendations experience, review the **Managed in** property and confirm that the value is **Defender**.
+- From cloud environment management, open the cloud **Environment management** page and confirm that the applicable environment is managed in Defender.
+
+[![Screenshot showing Defender portal in the Plans managed in column for an environment.](media/manage-exemptions-defender/environment-management-defender.png)](media/manage-exemptions-defender/environment-management-defender.png#lightbox)
+
+If a finding affects assets managed in Azure, you have two options:
+
+- Connect the environment to Defender and continue managing exemptions through Defender.
+- Create the exemption in Azure. For more information, see [Exempt resources from recommendations](/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/exempt-resource).
+
+### Permissions
+
+[Microsoft Defender unified role-based access control (RBAC)](/en-us/defender-xdr/manage-rbac) controls access to exemptions:
+
+| Role or permission | Access |
+| --- | --- |
+| Global Administrator or Security Administrator | Can view, create, edit, and delete exemptions across all existing and future scopes, including tenant-wide exemptions. |
+| Exposure Management (Manage) | Can create, edit, and delete exemptions for the scopes assigned to the user. Manage permission is required for every scope included in the rule. |
+| Exposure Management (Read) | Can view exemptions for assigned scopes but can't create, edit, or delete them. |
+
+To delegate exemption management, go to **System** > **Permissions** > **Microsoft Defender XDR** > **Roles** in the Microsoft Defender portal and create or update a role with the required permission and scope.
+
+[![Screenshot showing Security posture permissions for exemption management in Microsoft Defender unified RBAC.](media/manage-exemptions-defender/exemption-permissions.png)](media/manage-exemptions-defender/exemption-permissions.png#lightbox)
+
+## Create an exemption
+
+Go to **Exposure Management** > **Policies** > **Exemption**, and then select **Create Exemption**. The creation process includes four decisions:
+
+| Creation section | What you define | Key guidance |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Details and scope | The exemption name and the environments or assets to which the exemption applies. | Use the narrowest scope possible to represent the approved risk decision. Only Defender-managed environments and assets can be selected. Only Global Administrators and Security Administrators can create exemptions that apply to **All connected environments**. |
+| Conditions | The findings that the exemption applies to, such as specific recommendations, recommendation categories, or risk criteria. | Carefully review whether the condition is static or dynamic. Dynamic conditions can automatically apply to future findings that match the defined criteria, for example, all recommendations with a **Low** risk level. |
+| Justification and duration | The business justification, supporting evidence, and exemption duration. | Document the reason for accepting the risk, any compensating controls, and relevant evidence. Use a time-bound exemption with a defined review or expiration date. |
+| Review and create | The complete exemption configuration before submission. | Verify the selected scope and affected findings to ensure the exemption isn't broader than the approved business decision. |
+
+After the exemption is submitted, Microsoft Defender processes the exemption and updates matching findings. Changes to finding status, exposure calculations, and related posture metrics might not be reflected immediately.
+
+[![Screenshot showing the Name and scope step when creating an exemption in the Microsoft Defender portal.](media/manage-exemptions-defender/create-exemption-name-scope.png)](media/manage-exemptions-defender/create-exemption-name-scope.png#lightbox)
+
+## Create an exemption from a recommendation
+
+You can also create an exemption directly from a recommendation. When launched from a recommendation, Defender automatically prepopulates the exemption conditions based on the selected recommendation to reduce configuration effort and ensure the exemption targets the intended finding:
+
+[![Screenshot of the Create exemption and Manage in Azure portal actions for a security recommendation.](media/manage-exemptions-defender/create-exemption-from-recommendation.png)](media/manage-exemptions-defender/create-exemption-from-recommendation.png#lightbox)
+
+### What is prepopulated?
+
+- The exemption condition is automatically set to **By recommendation** and is based on the recommendation from which the exemption was created. This condition can't be changed during the creation flow.
+- The scope is automatically populated with the assets selected when the exemption was created. You can further refine, narrow, or expand the scope as needed before submitting the exemption.
+
+If the selection includes both Defender-managed and Azure-managed assets, the Defender exemption applies only to the supported Defender-managed assets. Manage the remaining assets in Azure or move the relevant environment to Defender management.
+
+Tip
+
+If your goal is to exempt all assets that currently have a specific recommendation, switch to the **By recommendation title** view before creating the exemption. This makes it easier to review all impacted assets and apply a consistent exemption decision across the entire recommendation set.
+
+## Manage exemption lifecycle
+
+Use the **Exemption rules** page to review the organization's exemption decisions and manage their lifecycle.
+
+- Edit a rule when its scope, matching conditions, justification, owner, or review period changes.
+- Delete a rule when the exception is no longer valid and matching findings should return to active remediation tracking.
+- Review expiring rules before the approved risk period ends.
+- Review expired rules as historical evidence of previous decisions and determine whether a new assessment is required.
+
+Note
+
+If multiple exemptions apply to the same recommendation, the recommendation remains exempted until the last active exemption expires or is removed, regardless of whether the exemption was created in Azure or in Microsoft Defender.
+
+When an exemption is deleted or reaches its expiration date, Microsoft Defender automatically re-evaluates the affected findings. Any findings that still require remediation return to an **Active** state and once again contribute to posture and risk calculations. Findings that are no longer applicable remain unaffected.
+
+## Understand the effect of an exemption
+
+When an exemption is active, matching findings are marked as **Exempted**. The exemption changes how the finding is treated, but it doesn't remove the finding, its supporting evidence, or its relationship to other security signals.
+
+Exempted findings remain available throughout Microsoft Defender investigation and drill-down experiences. Depending on the current filters, exempted findings might be hidden by default. To review them, update the status filter to include **Exempted** findings.
+
+### Score impact
+
+Exempted findings are excluded from the applicable security score calculations while the exemption remains active. The impact on the score depends on the exemption scope and the product experience.
+
+### Attack paths
+
+Exempting a recommendation doesn't remove it from associated attack paths. Microsoft Defender continues to include the recommendation in attack path analysis and clearly identifies it as **Exempted**. This helps security teams understand the potential impact of the accepted risk, maintain visibility into how the recommendation contributes to overall exposure, and reassess the exemption if the security posture or business requirements change.
+
+## Existing Azure exemptions and the transition to Defender
+
+This section is primarily relevant for organizations that historically managed recommendations and exemptions in Azure and are now transitioning their environments to be **Managed in Defender**. During this transition, Microsoft preserves existing Azure exemption configurations while establishing Defender as the central location for managing new exemption decisions.
+
+### How exemption ownership works
+
+Microsoft Defender and Azure can coexist during the transition period. While exemption rules remain owned by the portal where they were originally created, recommendation status remains consistent across experiences.
+
+- Exemption rules created in Azure continue to be managed in Azure.
+- Exemption rules created in Defender are managed from the **Exemption rules** page in Defender.
+- Exemption rule definitions aren't synchronized or copied between Azure and Defender.
+- Both Azure and Defender exemptions affect the corresponding recommendations.
+- Recommendation status and exemption state remain consistent regardless of which portal owns the exemption rule.
+
+### Existing Azure exemptions
+
+When an environment becomes **Managed in Defender**, Microsoft continues to honor exemption rules that were previously created in Azure.
+
+- Existing Azure exemptions continue to influence recommendation status and posture calculations.
+- Security teams can continue to edit or remove these exemptions in Azure.
+- These Azure-created exemptions don't appear as manageable exemption rules in Defender.
+
+This approach allows organizations to move to Defender without disrupting existing risk-acceptance decisions or requiring immediate migration of historical exemption rules.
+
+### Creating new exemptions
+
+After an environment becomes **Managed in Defender**, new exemptions for that scope must be created in Defender. New Azure exemptions can't be created for those scopes through the supported portal experience.
+
+This ownership model gives security teams centralized control over new exemption decisions while preserving existing Azure configurations. It also prevents teams from creating new, competing rules for the same Defender-managed scope in different portals.
+
+## Limitations
+
+The following limitations apply to exemption management in the Microsoft Defender portal:
+
+- Existing Azure exemptions continue to be honored after an environment is managed in Defender, but they aren't automatically migrated to the Defender portal.
+- Processing, status updates, score recalculation, and cross-portal status propagation aren't immediate and require additional processing time.
+
+## Why use exemption management in Microsoft Defender?
+
+Organizations that choose to manage their cloud posture in Microsoft Defender can benefit from a centralized exemption management experience integrated directly into the entire exposure management workflow. Azure continues to support exemption management, while Defender offers a unified experience for organizations looking to manage security posture across all workloads and related decisions from a single location.
+
+- **Flexible scopes**: Defender enables organizations to create exemptions across supported environments and assets, providing more flexibility in scope selection than traditional Azure hierarchy-based scoping.
+- **Reduced administrative overhead**: Centralized and reusable exemption rules help reduce the number of exemptions that need to be created and maintained across multiple Azure subscriptions, management groups, and scopes.
+- **Granular security permissions**: Microsoft Defender XDR unified RBAC enables organizations to separate read and manage permissions and delegate exemption management to specific security teams without relying solely on Azure administrative roles.
+- **Lifecycle governance by design**: While Azure also supports exemption management, Defender provides a more security-focused governance experience. Exemptions include review periods and mandatory expiration dates, making temporary risk-acceptance decisions easier to track, review, and validate during audits and compliance assessments. Security teams can easily identify exemptions that are approaching expiration, review expired exemptions, and periodically reassess accepted risks.
+- **Faster exemption processing**: Exemptions created in Defender are typically reflected in recommendation status, score calculations, and related experiences faster than equivalent exemptions in Azure. Microsoft continues to improve processing efficiency to further reduce the time required for exemption changes to take effect.

+# Manage posture policies - Microsoft Security Exposure Management | Microsoft Learn
+
+Posture policies define which security posture recommendations are evaluated and the scope in which they apply. Organizations can configure policies across different environments to align recommendation evaluation with their business, compliance, and operational requirements.
+
+Note
+
+Posture Policies are currently available only for **Cloud resources**.
+
+## Why use posture policies?
+
+Posture policies help organizations tailor Microsoft's default security recommendations to match their specific security, compliance, and operational requirements. While the Microsoft baseline provides a strong starting point, organizations often need additional flexibility to define which security rules should be evaluated, customize rule parameters, or adjust recommendation coverage for different environments.
+
+By using posture policies, security teams can apply stricter requirements to highly sensitive environments, add organization-specific or compliance-driven rules, and reduce unnecessary noise in lower-risk environments. This helps ensure that recommendations are aligned with business priorities, regulatory obligations, and the security posture expected for each environment, resulting in more relevant and actionable findings.
+
+## Before you begin
+
+### Verify that an environment is managed in Defender
+
+Policies created in Defender apply only to environments managed in Defender. You can verify the management location in either of the following ways:
+
+- From the recommendations experience, review the **Managed in** property and confirm that the value is **Defender**.
+- From cloud environment management, open the cloud **Environment management** page and confirm that the applicable environment is managed in Defender.
+
+[![Screenshot showing Defender portal in the Plans managed in column for an environment.](media/manage-posture-policies-defender/environment-management-defender.png)](media/manage-posture-policies-defender/environment-management-defender.png#lightbox)
+
+If an environment is managed in Azure, you can connect the environment to Defender and continue managing posture policies through Defender or continue managing the applicable configuration in Azure.
+
+### Plans
+
+Posture policies are available only for environments that have an eligible Microsoft Defender plan enabled.
+
+- Only environments with an active eligible plan can be selected as a policy scope.
+- Environments without any enabled eligible plans aren't available for policy assignment.
+- If no plans are enabled across the organization, the Recommendation Policies experience isn't available.
+
+### Permissions
+
+[Microsoft Defender unified role-based access control (RBAC)](/en-us/defender-xdr/manage-rbac) controls access to recommendation policies:
+
+| Role or permission | Access |
+| --- | --- |
+| Global Administrator or Security Administrator | Can view, create, edit, enable, disable, and delete policies across all existing and future scopes, including tenant-wide policies. |
+| Core security settings (Manage) | Can create, edit, enable, disable, and delete policies for the scopes assigned to the user. Manage permission is required for every scope included in the policy. |
+| Core security settings (Read) | Can view policies and their configuration for assigned scopes but can't change them. |
+
+To delegate policy management, go to **System** > **Permissions** > **Microsoft Defender XDR** > **Roles** in the Microsoft Defender portal and create or update a role with the required permission and scope.
+
+[![Screenshot showing Core security settings permissions for posture policy management in Microsoft Defender unified RBAC.](media/manage-posture-policies-defender/posture-policy-permissions.png)](media/manage-posture-policies-defender/posture-policy-permissions.png#lightbox)
+
+## Understand policy types
+
+The Defender portal includes a Microsoft-managed baseline policy and supports custom recommendation policies.
+
+| Policy type | Purpose | Supported management actions |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| MDC Baseline Policy | Provides an out-of-the-box set of Microsoft-recommended security rules focused on improving an organization's security posture. | Enable or disable the policy and edit supported scope and parameters. The policy can't be deleted or renamed, and its rules and categories can't be changed. |
+| Custom policy | Defines organization-specific security requirements by combining selected rules, categories, scope, and parameters. | View, edit, enable, disable, and delete. |
+
+### MDC Baseline Policy
+
+The MDC Baseline Policy is a Microsoft-managed policy that provides a recommended set of security posture rules based on Microsoft's security research, threat intelligence, and best practices. It is designed to help organizations strengthen their security posture by identifying and reducing common attack paths, misconfigurations, and exploitable exposures.
+
+Unlike compliance-focused frameworks that are primarily designed to satisfy regulatory requirements, the MDC Baseline Policy focuses on improving security outcomes and reducing risk. It delivers immediate posture value with minimal configuration and serves as the recommended starting point for most organizations.
+
+[![Screenshot showing the MDC security baseline policy details in the Microsoft Defender portal.](media/manage-posture-policies-defender/security-baseline-policy.png)](media/manage-posture-policies-defender/security-baseline-policy.png#lightbox)
+
+Key characteristics of the MDC Baseline Policy:
+
+- Microsoft manages and continuously updates the policy content to reflect evolving threats, security research, and best practices.
+- The policy is Microsoft-managed and intentionally provides limited customization. Organizations can modify rule parameters, change the assignment scope, edit parameters of rules, and enable or disable the policy, but the underlying set of Microsoft-recommended security controls is maintained by Microsoft.
+- The policy can't be deleted and can only be disabled when not required. Keeping the policy available ensures organizations can easily re-enable Microsoft's recommended security baseline without needing to recreate or reconfigure it.
+
+### Default assignment
+
+To help organizations realize security value immediately, the MDC Baseline Policy is assigned to **All connected environments** by default.
+
+- Existing connected environments are automatically included in the policy scope.
+- Newly connected environments are automatically assigned to the policy.
+- Organizations can modify the assignment and restrict the policy to selected environments when needed.
+
+## Create a custom policy
+
+Go to **Exposure Management** > **Policies**, and then select **Create policy**.
+
+[![Screenshot of the cloud scope options when creating a posture policy in the Microsoft Defender portal.](media/manage-posture-policies-defender/create-posture-policy-details-scope.png)](media/manage-posture-policies-defender/create-posture-policy-details-scope.png#lightbox)
+
+The creation process includes three main decisions:
+
+| Creation section | What you define | Key guidance |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Details and scope | The policy name, description, and Defender-managed environments to which the policy applies. | Select only environments that should follow the same security requirements. Only Global Administrators and Security Administrators can create policies that apply to all connected environments. |
+| Predefined rules and categories | Rules are individual security checks that generate recommendations. You can directly configure supported rule parameters, enable or disable individual rules, and tailor the policy to your organization's requirements. | Use predefined rules to select the security checks that are relevant to your organization's business, security, and compliance requirements. Configure supported rule parameters to align recommendations with internal policies, operational needs, and risk tolerance levels, while reducing unnecessary noise and focusing on the findings that matter most to your environment. |
+| Additional categories | Categories provide an additional set of Microsoft-defined recommendations grouped around a common security outcome. Unlike predefined rules, categories can't be customized or configured. Organizations can only choose whether to include or exclude a category from the policy. Category selections are additive and don't affect the predefined rule selections. | Microsoft recommends using both predefined rules and categories. Predefined rules provide granular control and customization, while categories provide broader coverage. Categories complement predefined rules rather than replace them. |
+
+[![Screenshot of the regulatory compliance framework filter during posture policy rule selection.](media/manage-posture-policies-defender/create-posture-policy-rules.png)](media/manage-posture-policies-defender/create-posture-policy-rules.png#lightbox)
+
+After the policy is created, Microsoft Defender runs applicable security assessments. New or updated recommendations are generated when assets in the selected scope don't meet the policy requirements. Policy processing and recommendation updates aren't immediate.
+
+## Compliance policies
+
+Microsoft supports compliance-related recommendations and maps recommendations to common regulatory frameworks, such as HIPAA, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and NIST. However, Recommendation Policies don't include out-of-the-box policies for specific compliance frameworks.
+
+This approach helps keep policy management streamlined by avoiding a large set of predefined compliance policies that might not be relevant to your organization. Instead, organizations can create targeted compliance-focused policies by selecting recommendations mapped to the regulatory frameworks they follow. This provides the flexibility to build compliance policies tailored to specific requirements while reducing unnecessary complexity and administrative overhead.
+
+To create a compliance-focused policy:
+
+1. Create a new policy.
+2. Assign the policy to the environments that are required to meet the selected compliance framework and regulatory requirements.
+3. Filter rules by the desired regulatory framework.
+4. Select all the rules.
+
+For more information, see [Assign regulatory compliance standards](/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/assign-regulatory-compliance-standards).
+
+## Rules management
+
+Use Rule Management when you need to understand how a specific recommendation is configured and applied across your organization. This view simplifies administration by providing a single place to track rule assignments, understand policy relationships, and manage rule configurations without navigating through multiple policies.
+
+[![Screenshot showing the Rules management page for posture policies in the Microsoft Defender portal.](media/manage-posture-policies-defender/posture-policy-rules-management.png)](media/manage-posture-policies-defender/posture-policy-rules-management.png#lightbox)
+
+## Understand the effect of a policy
+
+Posture policies determine which security checks are evaluated for selected assets. When an asset doesn't meet the requirements defined by an enabled policy, Microsoft Defender generates a recommendation to help address the identified security gap.
+
+If multiple policies apply to the same asset, a recommendation is generated whenever the asset fails the requirements of at least one applicable policy. When policy evaluations differ, the most restrictive outcome takes precedence.
+
+## Transition to Defender
+
+Organizations can continue to manage posture policies and security standards from both the Azure portal and the Microsoft Defender portal during the transition to **Managed in Defender**.
+
+Recommendations are evaluated across all applicable policy sources and surfaced consistently in both portals. This provides a single recommendation queue and prevents duplicate recommendations from being generated when the same security requirement is configured in multiple places.
+
+[![Screenshot showing Azure security policies with an option to go to Microsoft Defender for additional policies.](media/manage-posture-policies-defender/azure-security-policies-go-to-defender.png)](media/manage-posture-policies-defender/azure-security-policies-go-to-defender.png#lightbox)
+
+### Policy ownership
+
+Policy ownership remains with the portal where the policy or standard was created:
+
+- Security standards and policies created in Azure continue to be managed in Azure.
+- Policies created in Defender are managed from the **Posture policies** page in Microsoft Defender.
+- Policy definitions aren't synchronized or copied between Azure and Defender.
+- Recommendations generated by Azure and Defender configurations are surfaced in both supported experiences.
+
+### Managing recommendations
+
+Use the **Policy source** information on a recommendation to:
+
+- Understand whether the recommendation is driven by Azure, Defender, or both.
+- Navigate to the appropriate policy management experience.
+- Update, disable, or remove the policy configuration responsible for the recommendation.
+
+### Best practice for existing environments
+
+Microsoft recommends managing posture policies in Defender whenever possible and using Azure security policies only for scenarios that aren't currently supported in Defender, such as policies that require a Deny effect or [custom recommendations](/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/create-custom-recommendations).
+
+To reduce operational overhead and avoid overlapping policy management, disable Azure security standards that are no longer required for environments managed through Defender.
+
+For scenarios that require Azure-only capabilities, create dedicated Azure security standards containing only those controls. This approach enables organizations to centralize recommendation management in Defender while continuing to use Azure policies for capabilities that don't have an equivalent Defender experience.
+
+### Best practice for new subscriptions
+
+New Azure subscriptions inherit Azure security standards by default. When adopting Microsoft Defender as the primary posture management experience, review the Azure standards assigned to newly created subscriptions and disable any standards that you don't intend to manage from Azure.
+
+As long as Azure standards remain enabled, they can continue to generate recommendations alongside Defender-managed policies. Recommendations are surfaced as a single recommendation experience, and the **Policy source** field can be used to identify whether a recommendation originates from an Azure security standard, a Defender posture policy, or both.
+
+### Foundational CSPM
+
+Microsoft Defender doesn't include a free Foundational CSPM plan. Instead, it provides a single [Defender CSPM](/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/concept-cloud-security-posture-management) plan, which is a paid offering and the recommended Microsoft experience for posture management.
+
+Organizations that want to continue receiving posture recommendations in environments managed by Defender must enable Defender CSPM, even if they continue to manage policies and security standards from the Azure portal.
+
+Organizations that previously relied on Azure Foundational CSPM must enable Defender CSPM to continue receiving posture recommendations, even if policy and security standard management remains in the Azure portal. Without Defender CSPM, posture recommendations aren't generated for environments managed in Defender.
+
+## Limitations
+
+The following limitations apply to posture policy management in the Microsoft Defender portal:
+
+- Only Azure environments are supported.
+- Existing Azure policies continue to be honored but aren't automatically migrated to the Defender portal.
+- Custom recommendation creation isn't currently supported in Defender. [Custom recommendations](/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/create-custom-recommendations) can continue to be managed in Azure, and the resulting recommendations are visible in both Azure and Defender.
+- Defender posture policies currently support Audit-based recommendation evaluation only. Policy effects such as Deny aren't supported in Defender and must continue to be managed through Azure Policy.
+- Recommendation updates aren't immediate and require additional processing time. Microsoft continues to improve processing times across the posture management experience.
+
+## Why use policy management in Microsoft Defender?
+
+Azure continues to support its existing policy configuration capabilities, while Microsoft Defender provides a unified posture management experience across cloud, endpoint, identity, and other Defender-managed workloads. This enables security teams to manage posture requirements, recommendations, exposure insights, and related governance decisions from a single location.
+
+Organizations can transition posture policy management to Microsoft Defender and benefit from the following:
+
+- **Top-down policy management**: Define security requirements centrally and apply them consistently across the environments that require them.
+- **Reduced administrative overhead**: Reusable policies reduce repetitive configuration and simplify posture management across environments.
+- **Flexible security scopes**: Apply policies across Defender-managed environments without being limited to Azure resource hierarchy boundaries.
+- **Microsoft-managed baseline**: Start with the MDC Baseline Policy, which focuses on improving security posture and reducing exposure, then add custom policies only where business, security, or compliance requirements differ.
+- **Granular security permissions**: Use [Microsoft Defender unified RBAC](/en-us/defender-xdr/manage-rbac) to separate read and management permissions and delegate policy management to specific security teams.
+- **Cross-workload governance**: Manage posture requirements through a common experience across cloud, endpoint, identity, and other supported Defender workloads.
+- **Improved recommendation processing**: Policy and recommendation processing times are optimized for the Defender experience and continue to improve.

+If the recommendation still shows resources as unhealthy after 24 hours, see [Resolve an exemption that doesn't update the recommendation status](review-exemptions#resolve-an-exemption-that-doesnt-update-the-recommendation-status) for detailed steps.

+
+Exemptions help security teams focus on the risks that require action while maintaining a governed record of findings that don't require remediation. Use an exemption when a finding has been reviewed and determined to be a false positive, covered by another control, temporarily deferred, or accepted as risk. Each exemption records its scope, matching conditions, justification, and review period, helping your organization reduce operational noise without losing visibility or accountability.
+
+## Why use exemptions?
+
+Exemptions provide a structured alternative to informally suppressing a security finding. They help organizations:
+
+- Focus remediation resources on security findings that require action.
+- Apply a documented risk decision consistently across the relevant scope.
+- Reduce repetitive work by managing exceptions through centralized rules.
+- Record the justification and supporting context needed for governance, audit, and compliance.
+- Reassess accepted risks through expiration dates and lifecycle review.
+- Preserve the security context of exempted findings in investigation and attack-path experiences.
+
+## Use cases
+
+Create an exemption after a finding has been generated and reviewed, and your organization determines that remediation is not currently required. Common scenarios include:
+
+- The finding is a false positive.
+- The organization reviewed and accepted the risk.
+- A third-party control addresses the risk.
+- An alternative mitigation is already in place.
+- Remediation is deferred for a documented business or technical reason.
+
+## Remove a rule or create an exemption?
+
+Both recommendation policies and exemptions allow you to control recommendation behavior, but they serve different governance purposes. Use a policy change when a recommendation should not be evaluated for a specific scope. Use an exemption when the recommendation remains valid, but remediation is temporarily not required and should be tracked for governance, audit, or compliance purposes.
+
+| Action | What it does | Choose it when |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Remove the rule from a policy | Stops the rule from generating recommendations and findings for the selected policy scope. Assets within that scope will no longer be evaluated against the rule. | The recommendation is not relevant for the selected scope and should never apply there. This is a long-term policy decision that defines which security controls should be evaluated. Learn more in [Manage posture policies](/en-us/security-exposure-management/manage-posture-policies-defender). |
+| Create an exemption | Keeps the rule active and continues evaluating the finding, but marks matching findings as **Exempted** for the approved scope and review period. | The finding is valid, but remediation is temporarily postponed or accepted as an exception. Exemption preserves visibility, justification, ownership, and review tracking for governance, audit, and compliance needs. |
+
+## Before you begin
+
+### Verify that an environment is managed in Defender
+
+Exemptions created in Defender apply only to assets that belong to environments managed in Defender. You can verify the management location in either of the following ways:
+
+- From the recommendations experience, review the **Managed in** property and confirm that the value is **Defender**.
+- From cloud environment management, open the cloud **Environment management** page and confirm that the applicable environment is managed in Defender.
+
+If a finding affects assets managed in Azure, you have two options:
+
+- Connect the environment to Defender and continue managing exemptions through Defender.
+- Create the exemption in Azure.
+
+### Permissions
+
+[Microsoft Defender unified role-based access control (RBAC)](/en-us/defender-xdr/manage-rbac) controls access to exemptions:
+
+| Role or permission | Access |
+| --- | --- |
+| Global Administrator or Security Administrator | Can view, create, edit, and delete exemptions across all existing and future scopes, including tenant-wide exemptions. |
+| Exposure Management (Manage) | Can create, edit, and delete exemptions for the scopes assigned to the user. Manage permission is required for every scope included in the rule. |
+| Exposure Management (Read) | Can view exemptions for assigned scopes but can't create, edit, or delete them. |
+
+To delegate exemption management, go to **System** > **Permissions** > **Microsoft Defender XDR** > **Roles** in the Microsoft Defender portal and create or update a role with the required permission and scope.
+
+## Create an exemption
+
+Go to **Exposure Management** > **Policies** > **Exemption**, and then select **Create Exemption**. The creation process includes four decisions:
+
+| Creation section | What you define | Key guidance |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Details and scope | The exemption name and the environments or assets to which the exemption applies. | Use the narrowest scope possible to represent the approved risk decision. Only Defender-managed environments and assets can be selected. Only Global Administrators and Security Administrators can create exemptions that apply to **All connected environments**. |
+| Conditions | The findings that the exemption applies to, such as specific recommendations, recommendation categories, or risk criteria. | Carefully review whether the condition is static or dynamic. Dynamic conditions can automatically apply to future findings that match the defined criteria, for example, all recommendations with a **Low** risk level. |
+| Justification and duration | The business justification, supporting evidence, and exemption duration. | Document the reason for accepting the risk, any compensating controls, and relevant evidence. Use a time-bound exemption with a defined review or expiration date. |
+| Review and create | The complete exemption configuration before submission. | Verify the selected scope and affected findings to ensure the exemption isn't broader than the approved business decision. |
+
+After the exemption is submitted, Microsoft Defender processes the exemption and updates matching findings. Changes to finding status, exposure calculations, and related posture metrics might not be reflected immediately.
+
+## Create an exemption from a recommendation
+
+You can also create an exemption directly from a recommendation. When launched from a recommendation, Defender automatically prepopulates the exemption conditions based on the selected recommendation to reduce configuration effort and ensure the exemption targets the intended finding:
+
+### What is prepopulated?
+
+- The exemption condition is automatically set to **By recommendation** and is based on the recommendation from which the exemption was created. This condition can't be changed during the creation flow.
+- The scope is automatically populated with the assets selected when the exemption was created. You can further refine, narrow, or expand the scope as needed before submitting the exemption.
+
+If the selection includes both Defender-managed and Azure-managed assets, the Defender exemption applies only to the supported Defender-managed assets. Manage the remaining assets in Azure or move the relevant environment to Defender management.
+
+Tip
+
+If your goal is to exempt all assets that currently have a specific recommendation, switch to the **By recommendation title** view before creating the exemption. This makes it easier to review all impacted assets and apply a consistent exemption decision across the entire recommendation set.
+
+## Manage exemption lifecycle
+
+Use the **Exemption rules** page to review the organization's exemption decisions and manage their lifecycle.
+
+- Edit a rule when its scope, matching conditions, justification, owner, or review period changes.
+- Delete a rule when the exception is no longer valid and matching findings should return to active remediation tracking.
+- Review expiring rules before the approved risk period ends.
+- Review expired rules as historical evidence of previous decisions and determine whether a new assessment is required.
+
+Note
+
+If multiple exemptions apply to the same recommendation, the recommendation remains exempted until the last active exemption expires or is removed, regardless of whether the exemption was created in Azure or in Microsoft Defender.
+
+When an exemption is deleted or reaches its expiration date, Microsoft Defender automatically re-evaluates the affected findings. Any findings that still require remediation return to an **Active** state and once again contribute to posture and risk calculations. Findings that are no longer applicable remain unaffected.
+
+## Understand the effect of an exemption
+
+When an exemption is active, matching findings are marked as **Exempted**. The exemption changes how the finding is treated, but it doesn't remove the finding, its supporting evidence, or its relationship to other security signals.
+
+Exempted findings remain available throughout Microsoft Defender investigation and drill-down experiences. Depending on the current filters, exempted findings might be hidden by default. To review them, update the status filter to include **Exempted** findings.
+
+### Score impact
+
+Exempted findings are excluded from the applicable security score calculations while the exemption remains active. The impact on the score depends on the exemption scope and the product experience.
+
+### Attack paths
+
+Exempting a recommendation doesn't remove it from associated attack paths. Microsoft Defender continues to include the recommendation in attack path analysis and clearly identifies it as **Exempted**. This helps security teams understand the potential impact of the accepted risk, maintain visibility into how the recommendation contributes to overall exposure, and reassess the exemption if the security posture or business requirements change.
+
+## Existing Azure exemptions and the transition to Defender
+
+This section is primarily relevant for organizations that historically managed recommendations and exemptions in Azure and are now transitioning their environments to be **Managed in Defender**. During this transition, Microsoft preserves existing Azure exemption configurations while establishing Defender as the central location for managing new exemption decisions.
+
+### How exemption ownership works
+
+Microsoft Defender and Azure can coexist during the transition period. While exemption rules remain owned by the portal where they were originally created, recommendation status remains consistent across experiences.
+
+- Exemption rules created in Azure continue to be managed in Azure.
+- Exemption rules created in Defender are managed from the **Exemption rules** page in Defender.
+- Exemption rule definitions aren't synchronized or copied between Azure and Defender.
+- Both Azure and Defender exemptions affect the corresponding recommendations.
+- Recommendation status and exemption state remain consistent regardless of which portal owns the exemption rule.
+
+### Existing Azure exemptions
+
+When an environment becomes **Managed in Defender**, Microsoft continues to honor exemption rules that were previously created in Azure.
+
+- Existing Azure exemptions continue to influence recommendation status and posture calculations.
+- Security teams can continue to edit or remove these exemptions in Azure.
+- These Azure-created exemptions don't appear as manageable exemption rules in Defender.
+
+This approach allows organizations to move to Defender without disrupting existing risk-acceptance decisions or requiring immediate migration of historical exemption rules.
+
+### Creating new exemptions
+
+After an environment becomes **Managed in Defender**, new exemptions for that scope must be created in Defender. New Azure exemptions can't be created for those scopes through the supported portal experience.
+
+This ownership model gives security teams centralized control over new exemption decisions while preserving existing Azure configurations. It also prevents teams from creating new, competing rules for the same Defender-managed scope in different portals.
+
+## Limitations
+
+The following limitations apply to exemption management in the Microsoft Defender portal:
+
+- Existing Azure exemptions continue to be honored after an environment is managed in Defender, but they aren't automatically migrated to the Defender portal.
+- Processing, status updates, score recalculation, and cross-portal status propagation aren't immediate and require additional processing time.
+
+## Why use exemption management in Microsoft Defender?
+
+Organizations that choose to manage their cloud posture in Microsoft Defender can benefit from a centralized exemption management experience integrated directly into the entire exposure management workflow. Azure continues to support exemption management, while Defender offers a unified experience for organizations looking to manage security posture across all workloads and related decisions from a single location.
+
+- **Flexible scopes**: Defender enables organizations to create exemptions across supported environments and assets, providing more flexibility in scope selection than traditional Azure hierarchy-based scoping.
+- **Reduced administrative overhead**: Centralized and reusable exemption rules help reduce the number of exemptions that need to be created and maintained across multiple Azure subscriptions, management groups, and scopes.
+- **Granular security permissions**: Microsoft Defender XDR unified RBAC enables organizations to separate read and manage permissions and delegate exemption management to specific security teams without relying solely on Azure administrative roles.

 # Security policies in Microsoft Defender for Cloud - Microsoft Defender for Cloud | Microsoft Learn
 
+::: zone pivot="azure-portal"
+
 Security policies in Microsoft Defender for Cloud define how your cloud resources are evaluated for security across Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). A policy specifies the standards, controls, and conditions Defender for Cloud uses to assess resource configurations and identify potential security risks.
 
 Each policy includes [security standards](concept-regulatory-compliance-standards), which define the controls and assessment logic applied to your environment. Defender for Cloud continuously evaluates your resources against these standards. When a resource doesn’t meet a defined control, Defender for Cloud generates a security recommendation that describes the issue and the actions required to remediate it.
@@ -84,4 +93,191 @@ Learn more about [creating custom recommendations](create-custom-recommendations
 
 MCSB includes multiple controls that define expected security configurations. One of these controls is “Storage accounts should restrict network access using virtual network rules.”
 
-Defender for Cloud continuously assesses resources. If it finds any that don’t satisfy this control, it marks them as noncompliant and triggers a recommendation. In this case, the guidance is to harden Azure Storage accounts that aren't protected with virtual network rules.
\ No newline at end of file
+Defender for Cloud continuously assesses resources. If it finds any that don’t satisfy this control, it marks them as noncompliant and triggers a recommendation. In this case, the guidance is to harden Azure Storage accounts that aren't protected with virtual network rules.
+
+::: zone-end
+
+::: zone pivot="defender-portal"
+
+Posture policies define which security posture recommendations are evaluated and the scope in which they apply. Organizations can configure policies across different environments to align recommendation evaluation with their business, compliance, and operational requirements.
+
+## Why use posture policies?
+
+Posture policies help organizations tailor Microsoft's default security recommendations to match their specific security, compliance, and operational requirements. While the Microsoft baseline provides a strong starting point, organizations often need additional flexibility to define which security rules should be evaluated, customize rule parameters, or adjust recommendation coverage for different environments.
+
+By using posture policies, security teams can apply stricter requirements to highly sensitive environments, add organization-specific or compliance-driven rules, and reduce unnecessary noise in lower-risk environments. This helps ensure that recommendations are aligned with business priorities, regulatory obligations, and the security posture expected for each environment, resulting in more relevant and actionable findings.
+
+## Before you begin
+
+### Verify that an environment is managed in Defender
+
+Policies created in Defender apply only to environments managed in Defender. You can verify the management location in either of the following ways:
+
+- From the recommendations experience, review the **Managed in** property and confirm that the value is **Defender**.
+- From cloud environment management, open the cloud **Environment management** page and confirm that the applicable environment is managed in Defender.
+
+If an environment is managed in Azure, you can connect the environment to Defender and continue managing posture policies through Defender or continue managing the applicable configuration in Azure.
+
+### Plans
+
+Posture policies are available only for environments that have an eligible Microsoft Defender plan enabled.
+
+- Only environments with an active eligible plan can be selected as a policy scope.
+- Environments without any enabled eligible plans aren't available for policy assignment.
+- If no plans are enabled across the organization, the Recommendation Policies experience isn't available.
+
+### Permissions
+
+[Microsoft Defender unified role-based access control (RBAC)](/en-us/defender-xdr/manage-rbac) controls access to recommendation policies:
+
+| Role or permission | Access |
+| --- | --- |
+| Global Administrator or Security Administrator | Can view, create, edit, enable, disable, and delete policies across all existing and future scopes, including tenant-wide policies. |
+| Core security settings (Manage) | Can create, edit, enable, disable, and delete policies for the scopes assigned to the user. Manage permission is required for every scope included in the policy. |
+| Core security settings (Read) | Can view policies and their configuration for assigned scopes but can't change them. |
+
+To delegate policy management, go to **System** > **Permissions** > **Microsoft Defender XDR** > **Roles** in the Microsoft Defender portal and create or update a role with the required permission and scope.
+
+## Understand policy types
+
+The Defender portal includes a Microsoft-managed baseline policy and supports custom recommendation policies.
+
+| Policy type | Purpose | Supported management actions |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| MDC Baseline Policy | Provides an out-of-the-box set of Microsoft-recommended security rules focused on improving an organization's security posture. | Enable or disable the policy and edit supported scope and parameters. The policy can't be deleted or renamed, and its rules and categories can't be changed. |
+| Custom policy | Defines organization-specific security requirements by combining selected rules, categories, scope, and parameters. | View, edit, enable, disable, and delete. |
+
+### MDC Baseline Policy
+
+The MDC Baseline Policy is a Microsoft-managed policy that provides a recommended set of security posture rules based on Microsoft's security research, threat intelligence, and best practices. It is designed to help organizations strengthen their security posture by identifying and reducing common attack paths, misconfigurations, and exploitable exposures.
+
+Unlike compliance-focused frameworks that are primarily designed to satisfy regulatory requirements, the MDC Baseline Policy focuses on improving security outcomes and reducing risk. It delivers immediate posture value with minimal configuration and serves as the recommended starting point for most organizations.
+
+Key characteristics of the MDC Baseline Policy:
+
+- Microsoft manages and continuously updates the policy content to reflect evolving threats, security research, and best practices.
+- The policy is Microsoft-managed and intentionally provides limited customization. Organizations can modify rule parameters, change the assignment scope, edit parameters of rules, and enable or disable the policy, but the underlying set of Microsoft-recommended security controls is maintained by Microsoft.
+- The policy can't be deleted and can only be disabled when not required. Keeping the policy available ensures organizations can easily re-enable Microsoft's recommended security baseline without needing to recreate or reconfigure it.
+
+### Default assignment
+
+To help organizations realize security value immediately, the MDC Baseline Policy is assigned to **All connected environments** by default.
+
+- Existing connected environments are automatically included in the policy scope.
+- Newly connected environments are automatically assigned to the policy.
+- Organizations can modify the assignment and restrict the policy to selected environments when needed.
+
+## Create a custom policy
+
+Go to **Exposure Management** > **Policies**, and then select **Create policy**.
+
+The creation process includes three main decisions:
+
+| Creation section | What you define | Key guidance |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Details and scope | The policy name, description, and Defender-managed environments to which the policy applies. | Select only environments that should follow the same security requirements. Only Global Administrators and Security Administrators can create policies that apply to all connected environments. |
+| Predefined rules and categories | Rules are individual security checks that generate recommendations. You can directly configure supported rule parameters, enable or disable individual rules, and tailor the policy to your organization's requirements. | Use predefined rules to select the security checks that are relevant to your organization's business, security, and compliance requirements. Configure supported rule parameters to align recommendations with internal policies, operational needs, and risk tolerance levels, while reducing unnecessary noise and focusing on the findings that matter most to your environment. |
+| Additional categories | Categories provide an additional set of Microsoft-defined recommendations grouped around a common security outcome. Unlike predefined rules, categories can't be customized or configured. Organizations can only choose whether to include or exclude a category from the policy. Category selections are additive and don't affect the predefined rule selections. | Microsoft recommends using both predefined rules and categories. Predefined rules provide granular control and customization, while categories provide broader coverage. Categories complement predefined rules rather than replace them. |
+
+After the policy is created, Microsoft Defender runs applicable security assessments. New or updated recommendations are generated when assets in the selected scope don't meet the policy requirements. Policy processing and recommendation updates aren't immediate.
+
+## Compliance policies
+
+Microsoft supports compliance-related recommendations and maps recommendations to common regulatory frameworks, such as HIPAA, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and NIST. However, Recommendation Policies don't include out-of-the-box policies for specific compliance frameworks.
+
+This approach helps keep policy management streamlined by avoiding a large set of predefined compliance policies that might not be relevant to your organization. Instead, organizations can create targeted compliance-focused policies by selecting recommendations mapped to the regulatory frameworks they follow. This provides the flexibility to build compliance policies tailored to specific requirements while reducing unnecessary complexity and administrative overhead.
+
+To create a compliance-focused policy:
+
+1. Create a new policy.
+2. Assign the policy to the environments that are required to meet the selected compliance framework and regulatory requirements.
+3. Filter rules by the desired regulatory framework.
+4. Select all the rules.
+
+For more information, see [Assign regulatory compliance standards](/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/assign-regulatory-compliance-standards).
+
+## Rules management
+
+Use Rule Management when you need to understand how a specific recommendation is configured and applied across your organization. This view simplifies administration by providing a single place to track rule assignments, understand policy relationships, and manage rule configurations without navigating through multiple policies.
+
+## Understand the effect of a policy
+
+Posture policies determine which security checks are evaluated for selected assets. When an asset doesn't meet the requirements defined by an enabled policy, Microsoft Defender generates a recommendation to help address the identified security gap.
+
+If multiple policies apply to the same asset, a recommendation is generated whenever the asset fails the requirements of at least one applicable policy. When policy evaluations differ, the most restrictive outcome takes precedence.
+
+## Transition to Defender
+
+Organizations can continue to manage posture policies and security standards from both the Azure portal and the Microsoft Defender portal during the transition to **Managed in Defender**.
+
+Recommendations are evaluated across all applicable policy sources and surfaced consistently in both portals. This provides a single recommendation queue and prevents duplicate recommendations from being generated when the same security requirement is configured in multiple places.
+
+### Policy ownership
+
+Policy ownership remains with the portal where the policy or standard was created:
+
+- Security standards and policies created in Azure continue to be managed in Azure.
+- Policies created in Defender are managed from the **Posture policies** page in Microsoft Defender.
+- Policy definitions aren't synchronized or copied between Azure and Defender.
+- Recommendations generated by Azure and Defender configurations are surfaced in both supported experiences.
+
+### Managing recommendations
+
+Use the **Policy source** information on a recommendation to:
+
+- Understand whether the recommendation is driven by Azure, Defender, or both.
+- Navigate to the appropriate policy management experience.
+- Update, disable, or remove the policy configuration responsible for the recommendation.
+
+### Best practice for existing environments
+
+Microsoft recommends managing posture policies in Defender whenever possible and using Azure security policies only for scenarios that aren't currently supported in Defender, such as policies that require a Deny effect or [custom recommendations](/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/create-custom-recommendations).
+
+To reduce operational overhead and avoid overlapping policy management, disable Azure security standards that are no longer required for environments managed through Defender.
+
+For scenarios that require Azure-only capabilities, create dedicated Azure security standards containing only those controls. This approach enables organizations to centralize recommendation management in Defender while continuing to use Azure policies for capabilities that don't have an equivalent Defender experience.
+
+### Best practice for new subscriptions
+
+New Azure subscriptions inherit Azure security standards by default. When adopting Microsoft Defender as the primary posture management experience, review the Azure standards assigned to newly created subscriptions and disable any standards that you don't intend to manage from Azure.
+
+As long as Azure standards remain enabled, they can continue to generate recommendations alongside Defender-managed policies. Recommendations are surfaced as a single recommendation experience, and the **Policy source** field can be used to identify whether a recommendation originates from an Azure security standard, a Defender posture policy, or both.
+
+### Foundational CSPM
+
+Microsoft Defender doesn't include a free Foundational CSPM plan. Instead, it provides a single [Defender CSPM](/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/concept-cloud-security-posture-management) plan, which is a paid offering and the recommended Microsoft experience for posture management.
+
+Organizations that want to continue receiving posture recommendations in environments managed by Defender must enable Defender CSPM, even if they continue to manage policies and security standards from the Azure portal.
+
+Organizations that previously relied on Azure Foundational CSPM must enable Defender CSPM to continue receiving posture recommendations, even if policy and security standard management remains in the Azure portal. Without Defender CSPM, posture recommendations aren't generated for environments managed in Defender.
+
+## Limitations
+
+The following limitations apply to posture policy management in the Microsoft Defender portal:
+
+- Only Azure environments are supported.
+- Existing Azure policies continue to be honored but aren't automatically migrated to the Defender portal.
+- Custom recommendation creation isn't currently supported in Defender. [Custom recommendations](/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/create-custom-recommendations) can continue to be managed in Azure, and the resulting recommendations are visible in both Azure and Defender.
+- Defender posture policies currently support Audit-based recommendation evaluation only. Policy effects such as Deny aren't supported in Defender and must continue to be managed through Azure Policy.
+- Recommendation updates aren't immediate and require additional processing time. Microsoft continues to improve processing times across the posture management experience.
+
+## Why use policy management in Microsoft Defender?
+
+Azure continues to support its existing policy configuration capabilities, while Microsoft Defender provides a unified posture management experience across cloud, endpoint, identity, and other Defender-managed workloads. This enables security teams to manage posture requirements, recommendations, exposure insights, and related governance decisions from a single location.
+
+Organizations can transition posture policy management to Microsoft Defender and benefit from the following:
+
+- **Top-down policy management**: Define security requirements centrally and apply them consistently across the environments that require them.
+- **Reduced administrative overhead**: Reusable policies reduce repetitive configuration and simplify posture management across environments.
+- **Flexible security scopes**: Apply policies across Defender-managed environments without being limited to Azure resource hierarchy boundaries.
+- **Microsoft-managed baseline**: Start with the MDC Baseline Policy, which focuses on improving security posture and reducing exposure, then add custom policies only where business, security, or compliance requirements differ.
+- **Granular security permissions**: Use [Microsoft Defender unified RBAC](/en-us/defender-xdr/manage-rbac) to separate read and management permissions and delegate policy management to specific security teams.
+- **Cross-workload governance**: Manage posture requirements through a common experience across cloud, endpoint, identity, and other supported Defender workloads.
+- **Improved recommendation processing**: Policy and recommendation processing times are optimized for the Defender experience and continue to improve.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Microsoft Defender unified role-based access control (RBAC)](/en-us/defender-xdr/manage-rbac)
+- [Manage posture policies](/en-us/security-exposure-management/manage-posture-policies-defender)
+
+::: zone-end
\ No newline at end of file

messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 will add two new Advanced Hunting tables—SubmissionEvents and SubmissionResults—providing enhanced visibility into email submission activity. Public Preview starts mid-November 2026; General Availability begins late November 2026. No immediate action or compliance concerns are required.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated October 28, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and Why:

Microsoft Defender for Office 365 is introducing new email submissions data in Advanced Hunting in Microsoft Defender. The new submissions tables provide security operations teams with greater visibility into email submission activity and results, enabling analysts to query submission activity alongside other Defender data and build hunting and detection workflows tailored to their organization.

Rollout Schedule:

Public Preview (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 (previously early October 2026 and expect to complete by early December 2026 (previously early October).

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out late November 2026 (previously late October) and expect to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously mid-November).

Impact on Your Organization:

Who is affected:

- Security operations teams that use Advanced Hunting in Microsoft Defender.

- Admins and analysts who investigate email submissions and submission results.

Platforms/Services:

- Microsoft Defender for Office 365

- Microsoft Defender XDR

- Advanced Hunting

What will happen:

- Two new Advanced Hunting tables will be available: SubmissionEvents and SubmissionResults.

- SubmissionEvents provides information about email submission events.

- SubmissionResults provides information about the results associated with those submissions.

- Security teams can query submission information directly and correlate it with other Microsoft Defender XDR data.

- The tables can be used with Advanced Hunting custom detections, allowing organizations to create detections based on submission activity that is important to their SOC workflows.

Action Required/Recommendations:

No immediate action is required. Additional documentation for the new tables will be provided as part of the release.

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
